title: Annotatio III §.X (3)(a) cont.: Highest idolatry species — even without their Transsubstantiation hypothesis; God’s definition, not ours
pass_a_gloss: And by this itself the highest species of Idolatry is incurred — never denied even by the Pontificians themselves under a hypothesis of Transsubstantiation not made, and not to be denied apart from this hypothesis: both because they cannot be made more certain of their hypothesis by any argument of Revelation or of Reason, and by many arguments of either are at least rendered doubtful of it if not wholly led away from it; and because the nature and admission of Idolatry depends by no means on a human hypothesis and opinion, whether that be true or false, but truly on God’s determination or definition, by which we know idolatry properly so called is committed as often as that which is not the highest God, whether from error or without error, is either estimated or saluted as such, not to say affected with the highest religious cult.
pass_b_english: That is the highest species of idolatry — which even Pontificians never deny if Transsubstantiation is not supposed, and must not deny without that hypothesis.

They cannot make their hypothesis certain by Revelation or Reason; and idolatry turns on God’s definition, not on whether a human opinion is true or false — whenever what is not the highest God is estimated, saluted, or given highest cult as if it were.
source_text: Hôcque ipso summa Idololatriæ species incurritur, ne Pontificiis quidem ipsis, sub hypothesi haud facta Transsubstantiationis, negata unquam, sed nec neganda citra hanc hypothesin, tùm quod hypotheseos suæ nullo vel Revelationis vel Rationis argumento, certiores fieri possint, multis è contrario utriusque argumentis, saltem dubii de ista reddantur, si non omnino ab eadem abducantur; tùm, quod Idololatriæ natura ac admissio, neutiquam ab hypothesi opinioneque humana, sive vera ista sit, sive falsa, sed verò à determinatione seu definitione Dei, dependeat, quâ toties idololatriam propriè sic dictam committi novimus, quoties id, quod summe Deus non est, sive ex errore, sive citra errorem, vel æstimatur, vel salutatur talis, nedum religioso summôque cultu afficitur.
